Your statement, explained

Statement details and downloads

The problem

What did your card
actually cost you?

You can see your balance in the app. To find the interest, fees and rates, you may need to look across several pages of the statement.

Statement Check puts the figures it can identify in one place, with page references so you can check them yourself.

What you’ll see

Understand the numbers
that matter.

See the statement balance and what you were charged in interest and fees.

Find the annual rates, promotional expiry dates and minimum payment details shown on your PDF.

What you get

Your statement,
explained.

  1. 01

    Where you stand

    See what you owe, how your balance moved and when your minimum payment is due.

  2. 02

  3. 03

Explore the calculator with fictional figures.

Reading your results

Find the detail
behind the figures.

Each recognised figure includes the page number it came from. If a field is marked “Not identified”, you can check the original statement or ask your card provider.

You can print the summary, save it as PDF or download the figures as CSV or JSON.

Interest charged and annual rates

The interest charge is an amount in pounds for the statement period. An annual rate is a percentage listed by the card provider.

Find your PDF

Where is my
credit card statement?

01 · Open

Select your credit card.

Open the card provider’s app or online banking.

02 · Find

Look for Statements.

Try More or Manage card if it’s hidden.

03 · Save

Download the PDF.

Open the monthly statement and use Download or Share.

04 · Check

Choose your PDF.

Come back here and select the file you saved.

Privacy

Your PDF stays
on your device.

Read in your browser

Your statement is processed on your device.

Only the figures you need

The result uses recognised amounts, rates, dates and page numbers. It excludes names, addresses, account numbers and transaction descriptions.

Your copy to keep

The site stores neither your statement nor your result. Print or download the summary if you want to keep it.

Before you take the next step

A few
useful answers.

Which PDFs can I use?

Use a text-based UK credit card statement up to 15 MB and 30 pages. Scanned and password-protected PDFs are unsupported.

Is it free?

Yes. You can check one statement at a time and download the summary for free.

What if I can’t find the download in the app?

Try signing in to online banking in your browser and opening the Statements section for your credit card.
